title.narrative: Providing an Integrated Multi-Sector Humanitarian Response for Vulnerable Households Affected by Conflict in Syria

description.narrative: ltpgtSyria is now in its 14th year of crisis, grappling with an unprecedented emergency and new crises that continue to take a heavy toll on its people. EPDC suggests an intervention in Busra Esh-Sham sub-district and Hasakeh governorate to address the population’s basic needs and provide life-sustaining services. Assessments have highlighted the community's critical requirements across multiple sectors, notably WASH, Protection, and NFI. HNO 2024 reported that there are around 34,749 PIN in Busra Esh-Sham sub-district with an inter-sector severity score 4. As: NFI (22,665 PIN, severity 3), WASH (41,123 PIN, severity 4), and Protection (GBV: 12,317 PIN, severity 3 CP: 18,741 PIN, severity 4).lt/pgtltpgtAl-Hasakeh targeted SD: WASH(Ya'robiyah and Jawadiyah 46,580 PIN, severity 4) (Qahtaniyyeh 28,895 PIN, severity 3)ltbrgtlt/pgtltulgtltligtWASH:lt/ligtlt/ulgtltpgtIn Syria, access to WASH services has been severely affected by factors such as conflict, economic decline, power shortages, and climate change. This has resulted in limited access to clean water and sanitation facilities for the population. Approximately 13.56.M people, require WASH assistance. In Dara, 61% of the population faces insufficient water access, leading to the use of unsafe alternatives.ltbrgtTo address these challenges, the WASH project focuses on improving WASH conditions and alleviate the hardships faced by vulnerable people and increase resilience of affective communities, assured of safe, equitable and sustainable access to sufficient quantities of water by enhancing access to safe water through rehabilitation and improve productivity of 4 boreholes and installing solar energy systems(Simej borehole/Busra Esh-sham boreholes 1 and 2/The New Smaqiyat borehole) to ensure a reliable source of clean water. The project prioritizes areas with the greatest needs based on severity scale and SHF targeted areas.ltbrgtCost extension will be allocated entirely to the WASH sector to meet the high demand for assistance in NES.ltbrgtEPDC plans to rehabilitate and install solar energy systems for boreholes in 7 locations in Al-Hassakeh governorate.ltbrgtImplementation of the project follows established SOPs, including planning, reporting, procurement, and quality assurance. EPDC has extensive experience in similar projects and has an offices in a strategically located area in Dara and Hasakeh city to effectively reach communities in need.ltbrgtlt/pgtltulgtltligtNFI:lt/ligtlt/ulgtltpgtEPDC focuses on distributing heaters and vouchers for Tamaz fuel to a total of 1,350 households (6,750 individuals) outside of camps in multiple communities in the Busra Esh-Sham sub-district. Over the course of the winter season, each household will receive one heater and a total of 300 kg of Tamaz in three rounds. Utilizing Tamaz as an alternative to firewood is cost-efficient and environmentally friendly. EPDC will provide enough Tamaz to cover at least 50% of the monthly heating needs, allowing families to use heaters for approximately five to six hours per day.ltbrgtlt/pgtltulgtltligtProtection:lt/ligtlt/ulgtltpgtEPDC will establish a community center in Daraa, Busra Esh-Sham city, which will include a Women and Girls Safe Space (WGSS) and a Child-Friendly Space (CFS). Additionally, some activities will be implemented through a mobile team targeting the surrounding areas of Busra Esh-Sham. Services will include survivor-centered case management and psychosocial support, designed to ensure safety, confidentiality, and respect.ltbrgtThe project aims to address the unique challenges faced by survivors, such as early marriage, harassment, sexual abuse, and intimate partner violence, to enhance their physical and mental well-being. Community engagement and awareness-raising initiatives will challenge harmful practices and attitudes towards GBV, fostering a supportive environment for survivors.ltbrgtAdditionally, the project also aims to provide child protection services, including case management, psychosocial support, positive parenting for caregivers, awareness sessions about child protection, and training community members on child protection minimum standards.lt/pgtltpgtltbgtlt/bgtlt/pgt
